title: feat(plugin-form): record:line_items publishes every key of its 17.6.0 spec row, each by measurement (objectui#11536)
body:
Fixes #11536

Clause-②: yes

Why yes: the ten keys are declared on the block's registry `inputs`, which widens a published surface. The SDUI manifest, the JSX intrinsics and the page validator now accept them instead of reporting `unknown-prop`. The renderer does not change: it already read every one of them.

## What changed

- `packages/plugin-form/src/index.tsx`: the `line_items` registration declares the ten keys of the 17.6.0 `RecordLineItemsProps` row it did not publish (`parentObject`, `parentId`, `recordId`, `title`, `readonly`, `minRows`, `maxRows`, `filter`, `sort`, `limit`). `filter` and `sort` are `type: 'array'` with `of: 'object'`; `title` is `'string'` only, because the row declares a plain string and the panel draws it as a React child. Each input carries a description of what the panel does with it.
- New pin file `packages/plugin-form/src/__tests__/lineItemsDeclaredInputs-11536.test.tsx` (30 tests): the measurement every declaration rests on, plus the member pins for `columns`, `dataSource`, `filter` and `sort`.
- `apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts`: strikes every `OWED TO objectui#11536` entry (the ten unpublished keys and the two owed member pins), registers the four member pins in `MEMBER_PINS`, and lowers the caps those entries counted in (see "Shared cap line" below).
- `apps/console/src/__tests__/record-block-record-reach.test.tsx`: a file outside the claim's surface, added this round because this change turned it red (see "Deviation" below).
- `.changeset/11536-line-items-published-inputs.md`: `@object-ui/plugin-form` minor.

## The measurement, key by key

Method. A read in `LineItemsPanel` is not proof on its own: `SchemaRenderer` hoists the `properties` bag onto the node, and the block wraps the panel in `ElementDataSourceGate`. So each key is authored the way the spec authors it, as `{ type: 'record:line_items', properties: { … } }`. It is rendered through the real `SchemaRenderer` and this package's own registration, and asserted at what the key does: the query the adapter receives, the batch Save sends, or the DOM. Every row has a control beside it that differs only by that key. Read sites are named by symbol, per AGENTS.md #11.

| key | read site | measured effect (pin-file row) | declared |
|---|---|---|---|
| `parentObject` | `parentObject` const in `LineItemsPanel` (the key, else the page record's `objectName`), used by `save` for the rollup gate and `buildMasterDetailEditBatch`'s parent leg | names the parent leg of the Save batch: `{ object: 'purchase_order', action: 'update', id: 'p1', data: { total_amount: 5 } }`; outranks the page record's object; without it and with no page record, the batch has no parent leg | yes |
| `parentId` | `parentId` const (the key, else `recordId`, else the page record's `recordId`) → `load` (`find(childObject, { $filter: { [relationshipField]: parentId } })`) and `save` | `$filter: { po: 'p1' }`; a new line is saved with `po: 'p1'`; CONTROL: with no parent id, no `find` and the "Save the record first" state | yes |
| `recordId` | same `parentId` const, second in order | `$filter: { po: 'r9' }`; outranks the page record (`page-1`); loses to `parentId` | yes |
| `title` | `CardTitle` child: the key, else the `form.lineItems.title` default | heading reads "Order lines"; CONTROL "Line Items" | yes |
| `readonly` | Save button gate, `allow_add` / `allow_delete` in `gridField`, and the `readonly` prop on `LineItemsField` (`GridField` draws its read-only table) | no Save, no Add line / Duplicate row / Remove row, read-only table, no inputs; CONTROL: all present | yes |
| `minRows` | `gridField.min_rows` → `GridField`'s `minRows` (`removeRow` guard and Remove button `disabled`) | with 2 lines and `minRows: 2` both Remove row buttons are disabled; no blank lines are added; CONTROL: enabled | yes |
| `maxRows` | `gridField.max_rows` → `GridField`'s `maxRows` (`addRow` / `duplicateRow` guards, ghost row, Add and Duplicate `disabled`) | with 2 lines and `maxRows: 2`, Add line and Duplicate row are disabled and the entry row is gone (2 inputs, not 3); CONTROL: enabled, 3 inputs | yes |
| `filter` | `useResolvedFilter(schema.filter, …)` → `toFilterNodeSafely` → `mergeFilterNodes(parentScope, …)` in `load` | `$filter: ['and', ['po', '=', 'p1'], [['billable', 'equals', true]]]`; CONTROL `{ po: 'p1' }` | yes |
| `sort` | `convertSortToQueryParams(schema.sort)` → `$orderby` in `load` | `$orderby: { amount: 'desc' }`; CONTROL: no `$orderby` | yes |
| `limit` | `resolveRowLimit(schema.limit, DEFAULT_LINE_ITEMS_LIMIT)` → `$top` in `load` | `$top: 25`; CONTROL `$top: 500` | yes |

Keys left out: none. The row has fifteen keys. The other five (`childObject`, `relationshipField`, `columns`, `amountField`, `totalField`) were declared before this change and are not re-judged here, apart from the `childObject` note under Acceptance notes.

`filter` / `sort` / `limit` are TOP-LEVEL reads, not only `dataSource` members (PM hypothesis 2, measured). With no binding, `useElementDataSourceSchema` returns the schema by reference ("BY REFERENCE when there is nothing to apply") and the panel reads the three keys itself, which is what the rows above assert with no `dataSource` on the node. With a binding, the gate composes them first: the panel's own `filter` is ANDed with the binding's and the view's, and the panel's own `sort` / `limit` outrank the view's while losing to the binding's own (pinned in the `dataSource` block of the pin file).

## Member pins

| id | what the pin asserts |
|---|---|
| `record:line_items.columns` | one column per member in authored order, headed by `label` or else `name`; `type` picks the cell control and a typeless member is a text cell, with no hydration from the child object; `defaultHidden` hides a member, `required` outranks it and marks the header; `name` is the field Save writes |
| `record:line_items.dataSource` | `object` lands on `childObject` and outranks an authored one; `view` contributes filter (behind the parent scope), sort and page size; an unresolvable view reports and loads nothing; panel `sort` / `limit` outrank the view's, binding `sort` / `limit` outrank the panel's; binding `filter` is ANDed with the panel's; a view's `columns` are not read |
| `record:line_items.filter` | `ViewFilterRule` members reach `$filter` in order as one group ANDed behind the parent scope, operator word unchanged; a member naming the relationship field does not replace the scope; `[]` is no criterion |
| `record:line_items.sort` | `{ field, order }` members reach `$orderby` in authored order; a member with no `field` is dropped while siblings survive; an `order` other than `desc` reads ascending; no usable member sends no `$orderby` |

`filter` and `sort` entered the array-armed population by being declared, and were pinned in the same change, so `MEMBER_PIN_EXEMPTION_CEILING` goes to 0 rather than staying at 2.

## PM hypotheses, as measured

1. The ten keys: confirmed by the gate's own output. With the fix committed (`c9e2fe3`) and `index.tsx` reverted to the base `6158e4c93`, `record:line_items publishes every top-level key its spec props schema declares` received exactly `parentObject, parentId, recordId, title, readonly, minRows, maxRows, filter, sort, limit`.
2. Top-level versus `dataSource`-only: all three are read top-level (above).
3. `memberPins` names `columns` and `dataSource` on `main`: confirmed, and used.
4. End state: no `OWED TO objectui#11536` entry is left in any ledger. The owner stays in `OBJECTUI_11111_OWNERS` with a per-owner total of 0, the shape objectui#8652 and objectui#8649 left when they were struck.
- The brief's note that the parity test "reads built packages" did not hold. The console's vite config aliases `@object-ui/plugin-form` to its `src`, so the parity test reads source. The closure build was still needed, for `type-check`.

## Reverse validation (one-off, no file kept)

The fix was committed first (`c9e2fe3`). Then `packages/plugin-form/src/index.tsx` was replaced with the base blob under a `trap … EXIT INT TERM` restore. The mutation on disk: `grep -c "name: 'parentObject'"` 0, against 1 at HEAD. The parity test then went red, the expected direction: 2 failed / 253 passed. The two reds were the ten unpublished keys above and `every member pin names a key that is still array/object-armed on a covered block`, which received `record:line_items.filter` and `record:line_items.sort`. Restored with `git checkout HEAD -- …`, checked by blob hash equal to `HEAD:packages/plugin-form/src/index.tsx` (`ef2d497e`) and an empty `git diff HEAD`. With the fix: 255 / 255 green.

## Shared cap line (serial note for objectui#11068)

Changed in `registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts`:
- `OBJECTUI_11111_LEDGER_CAPS.unpublishedKeys` 12 → 2, removing objectui#11536's 10; objectui#11168's 1 and objectui#11068's 1 remain.
- `memberPins` 2 → 0.
- The per-owner totals: `'objectui#11536'` 12 → 0.
- `MEMBER_PIN_EXEMPTION_CEILING` 2 → 0.

Whichever of this PR and objectui#11068 lands second recomputes `unpublishedKeys` from the ledger. After both, it reads 1, which is objectui#11168's.

## Deviation: one file outside the claim's surface

`apps/console/src/__tests__/record-block-record-reach.test.tsx` went red under this change. Its sampler fills every declared input, and the newly declared `parentId` / `recordId` (sampled `'x'`) outrank the bound record. That is the declared behaviour, but it detached the panel from the record, so the probe reported "the bound record does not reach its output". The fix restates the renderer default, the key absent, for the three override keys in `SAMPLE_BY_INPUT`, beside the six defaults that table already restates for the same reason. It also annotates the docblock sentence "NO public block declares a `recordId` input", which this change made false. 13 / 13 green after the fix.

Lint is narrowed to the four changed TS files (`eslint --no-inline-config --format json`), a measurement rather than a skip:
- Population: the root `eslint.config.js` applies to every `**/*.{ts,tsx}`.
- Count: the JSON output holds 4 files, 0 errors and 33 warnings (`no-explicit-any` / `react-refresh/only-export-components`, the kinds the neighbouring code already carries).
- Invariance: the config enables no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project` / `projectService`), and no rule under `eslint-rules/` reads another file. So this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file.

The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's.

Docs: no page lists this block's inputs. The plugin-form README and the docs table name the block and its fallback only, and the manifest is generated from the registration, so no doc changes.

## Acceptance notes (not filed here)

1. `childObject` is declared `required: true`, while the 17.6.0 row declares it optional. The row's own description says why: the component-level `dataSource` binding can supply it. Measured once through the real `manifestFromConfigs` + `validateTree` pair: a node that binds the object through `dataSource` and omits `childObject` gets a `missing-required-prop` error on `childObject`. `RecordLineItemsProps.safeParse` accepts the same props, and the panel renders such a node (the `dataSource` pin rows). This is not changed here, because it is not one of the ten ruled keys. It is in the report for the seat.
2. `packages/types/src/zod/public-blocks.zod.ts` still says `record:line_items` has no spec row "on purpose". 17.6.0 carries the row, so the sentence went stale at the bump. Carrier: objectui#10872, which holds that arming.
3. A `ViewFilterRule` operator reaches `$filter` as written, so a word outside the spec's operator enum is forwarded too. The spec's authoring gate refuses such a word. Observation only.
